Aureus ERP through 1.6.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in HolidayAction.php that allows authenticated users to inject scripts via unescaped holiday names rendered as HtmlString. Attackers permitted to create Public Holidays or Mandatory Days can store JavaScript payloads that execute when HR managers or administrators open the Holiday modal, hijacking their sessions.

Aureus ERP through 1.6.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read unpublished draft blog posts via the customer-facing post view page. Attackers who know or guess a post slug can retrieve the full title, content, image, tags, author and publish date because PostResource skips authorization and ViewPost ignores is_published.

QloApps through 1.7.0 contains an improper access control vulnerability in AdminSlipController that allows hotel-restricted back-office employees to access credit slips of all hotels. Attackers can list, export as PDF, mark as redeemed, and generate store-credit vouchers from other hotels' refund records, exposing customer identities and amounts.

QloApps through 1.7.0 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows hotel-restricted back-office employees to create room types under unassigned hotels by supplying an arbitrary id_hotel. Attackers can enumerate all hotels via the unfiltered room type form selector and post foreign hotel IDs to AdminProductsController, creating rooms and inventory under other hotels.

QloApps through 1.7.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in AdminSearchConfController::processSave() that echoes rejected alias and search values unescaped in validation errors. Attackers can induce an authenticated back-office user to submit a crafted request, executing JavaScript in that user's administrative session.

QloApps through 1.7.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in AdminHotelRoomsBookingController::postProcess() that allows restricted back-office employees to access other hotels' data by supplying an id_hotel parameter. Attackers can modify the id_hotel URL parameter on the Book Now page to view room availability and booking status of hotels outside their assigned profile access.

QloApps through 1.7.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in AdminProductsController::ajaxProcessBulkUpdateRooms that allows hotel-restricted back-office employees to modify rooms of other hotels. Attackers can submit foreign room IDs in the id_rooms parameter to change status, floor, comments, or inactive dates, disrupting availability and bookings.

QloApps through 1.7.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the exceptions field of the back-office Transplant a module form. Attackers can craft a malicious link containing JavaScript payload in the exceptions parameter that executes in an authenticated administrator's session when the victim follows the link.

QloApps through 1.7.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the back-office Hotel Reservation System Book Now search, where date_to and id_room_type parameters are copied into template variables without validation. QloApps through 1.7.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the back-office room type editor that fails to escape room_num, floor, and comment field values in input attributes. Attackers can induce authenticated back-office users to submit crafted POST requests with malicious payloads to execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's administrative session.

QloApps through 1.7.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the back-office room type editor's length of stay fields. Attackers can induce authenticated administrators to submit crafted POST requests with malicious payloads in restriction_min_los and restriction_max_los parameters, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's administrative session.

Aureus ERP before 1.6.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the Chatter field-change log where old_value and new_value entries are rendered without proper escaping. Any user permitted to edit tracked text fields can inject malicious markup that executes when other users, including administrators, view the record's Chatter panel.

Aureus ERP through 1.6.0 stores the Payment Term note field unsanitized and renders it as raw HTML in the Accounting plugin. Authenticated users with payment-term create permission can submit arbitrary JavaScript to the payment-terms endpoint, which persists to the database and executes in browsers of all users viewing that Payment Term record.

QloApps through 1.7.0 reflects unescaped child feature names into back-office validation error messages in the Hotel Reservation System feature management page. Authenticated back-office users who follow a crafted link can execute injected JavaScript in their administrative session via the child_features parameter.

QloApps through 1.7.0 renders back-office list filter POST parameters into HTML input value attributes without escaping them in the list helper template. Attackers can induce authenticated users to submit crafted POST requests with malicious payloads to list controllers, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's session to read administrative data and perform actions.
